elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase, minimum volume, or take-or-pay commitment.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly states: “Customer makes no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment.” Section 12.3 is consistent with this position.

elements.element: Customer is required to pay fees only for Services it has ordered or actually used.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 states that Customer is obliged to pay only for Services ordered under a signed Order Form or actually used.

elements.element: If a minimum commitment applies, it is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Section 2.1 expressly eliminates all minimum purchase, volume, and take-or-pay commitments; therefore, no commitment extends beyond the current 12-month term.

elements.element: If a minimum commitment applies, Customer may reduce it on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the operative clause imposes no minimum commitment requiring a reduction right.

elements.element: If a minimum commitment applies and Customer has a shortfall, the remedy is a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the operative clause imposes no minimum commitment and therefore creates no commitment shortfall, penalty, or required true-up.

result.reason: The operative redline fully adopts the preferred position by eliminating the three-year take-or-pay obligation and limiting payment obligations to ordered or used Services. It also resolves the contradiction with Section 12.3. The fallback protections are satisfied because their triggering condition—a minimum commitment—is expressly absent. The revision is targeted to the disputed commitment and introduces no unrelated commercial obligation.
